title: Multi-Agent Operating Discipline for Teams
promise: Enable a technically literate engineering lead or solo operator who already runs a flat-rate agentic coding subscription to dispatch, steer, and recover more than one AI coding agent at a time without the failure modes that cost other teams redone work, silently overwritten files, and false 'done' claims.
audience: engineering leads, solo technical founders, and developers already paying for Claude Code, Codex, or a comparable agentic coding tool who run more than one agent at a time

competencies.description: Write a complete agent brief that states the requested outcome, exact scope, the permitted operation, and what 'done' measures, so a subagent with no memory of the conversation cannot go astray.
Recognize the fan-out anti-pattern and decide when splitting work across several agents changes the answer versus wasting tokens and time for no gain.
Steer a running agent mid-flight and recover an interrupted commission without redoing finished work or starting a second writer that collides with a still-running peer.
Use dated receipts and lifecycle journaling as inter-session memory so the next session, or the next agent, does not have to re-derive what a prior one already established.
Coordinate two or more concurrent agent sessions sharing one working tree without silent collisions, using division-by-message and path manifests rather than luck.

lessons.title: The Complete Brief: What a Subagent Must Be Told
deliverables: a live brief written against the participant's own real backlog item

lessons.title: The Fan-Out Anti-Pattern
deliverables: a worked before/after split of a broad task the participant brought in

lessons.title: Steering, Interrupting, and Recovering a Running Agent
deliverables: a recovery runbook for an interrupted commission
a live steering exercise against a real running agent

lessons.title: Receipts and Lifecycle Journaling as Inter-Session Memory
deliverables: a minimal dated-receipt convention the participant can adopt this week
a worked example distinguishing a receipt from a transcript

lessons.title: Case Study: From Collision to Coordination — Two Concurrent Sessions, One Checkout
deliverables: a coordination protocol (path manifests, division-by-message) the participant's team can adopt

correctionPolicy: append a new course revision; never edit admitted lesson truth in place
